notes: Defects span all four lenses and three severities. D1, D2 and D7 are the ones that would actually sink the project.

defects.description: The event shape is a public integration contract for three partners, with no version field, no versioning strategy, and no compatibility policy.
defects.detection_criteria: Review identifies the event schema as a one-way door once partners consume it, or raises the absence of schema versioning / evolution strategy.

defects.description: Notifications table has no tenant or partner scoping column despite external partners publishing to the topic. Retrofitting tenancy onto a table retained indefinitely requires a backfill.
defects.detection_criteria: Review flags the absence of tenancy/partner scoping in the data model, or notes the schema is a one-way door requiring backfill to change.

defects.description: Provider throughput is asserted as fact and the load test against SendGrid is scheduled last, in week 8, after all six services have migrated.
defects.detection_criteria: Review identifies the provider throughput claim as an untested assumption, or objects that the load test is sequenced after migration rather than before.

defects.description: No do-nothing option, no buy-instead-of-build option, and no option to extend an existing service. Only the queue vendor choice has alternatives at all.
defects.detection_criteria: Review notes the absence of a do-nothing, buy, or extend-existing alternative for the central build-a-new-service decision.

defects.description: Inverted attention: a long, well-reasoned section on the reversible queue vendor choice, while the irreversible event contract and data model pass without discussion.
defects.detection_criteria: Review explicitly contrasts the depth spent on the queue choice against the depth spent on schema or event contract.

defects.description: Latency and availability are stated as 'fast' and 'highly available' with no percentile, no measurement point, and no target.
defects.detection_criteria: Review flags the performance language as unquantified and asks for a percentile or numeric target.

defects.description: No delivery semantics: at-least-once versus exactly-once is unstated, and there is no deduplication or idempotency key, despite SQS standard queues delivering duplicates.
defects.detection_criteria: Review raises duplicate delivery, idempotency, or missing delivery-guarantee semantics.

defects.description: The build-our-own-queue alternative is a strawman, dismissed as obviously impractical with no analysis.
defects.detection_criteria: Review identifies the self-built queue option as a strawman or notes it was dismissed without reasoning.

defects.description: Indefinite retention of every notification row with no cost ceiling, no retention policy, and no consideration of deletion obligations.
defects.detection_criteria: Review raises retention, unbounded table growth, storage cost, or data deletion obligations.

defects.description: No rollback path. Once six services publish events instead of sending directly, there is no described way back.
defects.detection_criteria: Review raises the absence of a rollback or migration-reversal path.
